name: Custom home
summary: One-off architect-designed detached home on the owner's lot, priced per finished SF. Cost is driven by design complexity, finishes, glazing, site conditions (slopes, hillside foundations) and region. Census contract-price data gives a solid national floor ($172 median, $198 average per SF, 2025), but it covers all contractor-built homes, including plan-book houses. Architect-designed work runs higher. The default mid is a derived premium over the Census average; the only architect-grade evidence is from high-cost Los Angeles fire rebuilds.

typicalSize.method: Census 2025 contractor-built completions: median 2,433 SF, average 2,773 SF (e5). Architect-designed homes skew larger, so the mid is set at ~1.25× the average. High covers estate homes. The low/high are judgment.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Garage spaces per finished SF. A 2–3 car garage on a ~3,500 SF home ≈ 0.0008 spaces/SF. Garage area is not in finished SF but its cost is inside the hard cost.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Per finished SF. Low ≈ Census 2025 contractor-built median contract price ($171.57/SF, e1), rounded up for an architect-designed scope. Mid = Census 2025 average ($198.33/SF, e1) × ~1.3 for one-off architect-designed complexity (custom glazing, millwork, structure, more site work) ≈ $258, rounded to $260. The 1.3 premium is a judgment, not sourced. High $450 ≈ national luxury and high-cost-region custom work. LA fire-rebuild custom homes run $500/SF (LA County budget, e3) to $640–710/SF (design-builder, e4) in CA-LosAngeles dollars, which regionalize down to roughly $400–550 nationally. Census custom median/average by region (e1): NE $179/$246, MW $194/$202, South $157/$180, West $177/$214.

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. general conditions and OH&P for the house, attached garage, typical on-lot work (excavation, driveway, flatwork, utility laterals, basic landscaping). Excludes land, design fees, permits, special foundations (caissons/retaining on hillside lots), pools, wells/septic, solar, wildfire hardening and FF&E (see line items). Census contract prices exclude the lot.

qualityTiers.method: Economy ≈ Census median contract price / mid (172/260 ≈ 0.66, rounded to 0.7). Premium/luxury are judgment: $350 and $455/SF nationally. Luxury ≈ the regionalized LA rebuild evidence (e3, e4).

systemSplit.method: Starts from the production single-family split (NAHB 2024 Table 1 mapped to CSI). Adjustments, all judgment: Div 01 up to 14% (one-off GC supervision and higher fee); 08 up to 7% (more and larger glazing); 11 and 12 up (premium appliances and custom cabinetry); 04 and 05 up slightly (veneer, steel beams for open spans); 06, 09, 22 and 32 trimmed to keep the sum at 1.000.

lineItems.name: Fire-code and wildfire-resilience upgrades (WUI zones)

cost.method: LA County Altadena budget (e3): fire code upgrades $40,000 + fire-resilient upgrades $25,740 = $65,740 (high). Low = the resilience upgrades alone. Mid ≈ midpoint, rounded.

lineItems.notes: Only in wildland-urban-interface or high fire-hazard zones.

lineItems.name: Rooftop solar PV system

cost.method: Mid = LA County Altadena budget line ($15,200, e3) for a 1,650 SF home. Low/high is a judgment for system size.

lineItems.notes: Required for new homes under California Title 24; optional elsewhere.

lineItems.name: Underground utility service connection

cost.method: Mid = LA County Altadena line 'Utilities Undergrounding Connection $20,000' (e3). Low/high is a judgment.

lineItems.notes: Where overhead service must be undergrounded to the house.

lineItems.name: Hillside caisson foundations and retaining walls

cost.method: Letter Four: 'Caisson foundations and retaining walls can add $100K–$300K' on hillside lots (e4). Mid ≈ midpoint, rounded down.

lineItems.notes: Steep or geotechnically difficult lots only.

cost.method: Fixr 3-bedroom septic range (single-family e11). Engineered/mound systems can exceed this.

pctOfHard.method: LA County Altadena budget (e6): architecture & design 10–15% of construction ($82,500), soils/survey/civil $8,450, permits $21,500. That is $112,450 = 12.1% of the $925,940 construction subtotal, plus financing & legal $109,594 (11.8%), for 24% total. Letter Four (e7) puts design & engineering at 12–18% of hard cost. Mid 22% = A&E ~13% + permits/surveys ~3% + financing/legal/insurance ~6%. Low assumes a design-build or stock-plan basis and cash funding. High = full-service architecture + interior design + construction loan. | Second pass (2026-10-24, main session): Reduced 4 points to remove construction-loan financing; developer fee 0 (owner-built). The engine adds impact & tap fees, the developer fee and construction financing as their own lines (docs/BUDGET_ENGINE.md §5), so this bucket must exclude them.

softCosts.notes: Owner-builder custom homes carry no developer overhead or sales costs. Full architectural service (10–18%) dominates soft cost.

developerFee.method: Owner-built custom home: no developer fee.

design.method: One-off designs change during documentation. A judgment above production-home norms; no type-specific source found.

hard.method: Letter Four advises to 'Budget 10–15% above your estimate' for custom rebuilds (e7). Low 5% for fully bid, simple designs.

soft.method: General development norm; no type-specific source found.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Per finished SF, hard + soft, excl. land. Min ≈ $172 Census median × 1.1 soft. Max ≈ LA hillside/luxury rebuilds ($640–930 hard per e4) plus soft costs. National luxury rarely exceeds $1,000/SF all-in outside the top coastal markets.

source.title: Characteristics of New Housing — Median and Average Contract Price per Square Foot of New Contractor-Built Single-Family Houses Started (contractpricesqft_cust.xls)

evidence.quote: Sheet ContractMedAvgPriceSqFt, row 2025: United States median 171.57, average 198.33; Northeast 179.3 / 246.26; Midwest 194.09 / 202.13; South 157.3 / 179.96; West 176.87 / 213.85
evidence.scopeNotes: Contract price to a general contractor for a home on the owner's land (excludes improved lot). Covers all contractor-built homes, not only architect-designed ones. Likely excludes the owner's separate design fees.

evidence.quote: For custom single-family detached (SFD) homes started in 2025, the median price climbed to $171 per square foot.
evidence.scopeNotes: NAHB analysis of the same Census data as e1. The custom premium over spec homes (lot excluded) was 12.6%.

evidence.scopeNotes: Builder marketing guide (Q2 2026) for WUI-compliant custom homes, hard cost before soft costs. High-cost market with post-fire demand surge.

openQuestions: No national source isolates architect-designed custom homes. The 1.3× premium over the Census contractor-built average is a judgment; custom-builder association surveys (e.g., NAHB Custom Builder Council) or RSMeans 'Custom' class square-foot models would anchor it.
Census contract prices may or may not include site work and design fees for each home; scope varies by contract.
